I've been working this land for thirty years. My father farmed it before me. I know this soil, I know when the rains come and when they don't, and I know what the well can give me. I don't need a piece of paper to tell me how to farm — I watch my neighbors, I remember what worked last year and the year before.

My land is 10.9 mu. The main fields — about 6 mu — I run wheat in winter and maize in summer, same as always. That's the backbone. After I pull the wheat in June, I get maize in the ground quick so I don't lose the season. The other nearly 5 mu I put into vegetables: eggplant, tomato, watermelon. That's where I make real money at the market. Two people can manage this.

For seeds, I buy the hybrid maize and hybrid vegetable seeds from the county supply store — everyone does now, the yields are just better. For wheat I use the improved variety I've been buying for years, I know it does well here.

Fertilizer, I put more than maybe I should, but I'd rather not lose the crop. I put it on at planting and top-dress when the plants need it. I irrigate from my well — wheat needs four waterings, maize three, vegetables need more because summers get hot and dry here in Hebei. I spray for pests and disease when I see problems starting, same schedule I've always followed.

Tillage is rotary on everything except after wheat harvest — there I go straight in with the maize seed, no time to waste.
